This period defined my year at both Quillfeather and Altimetry, focusing on delivering zero-error migrations while building essential tools for incident response and developer experience. I shipped critical reliability improvements across billing and internal platforms that reduced operational noise and accelerated onboarding.

## Billing Migration and Stability
I led the cutover to the new ledger system at Quillfeather by writing a PR that flipped the read path to the new ledger, which moved 41k subscriptions off the legacy invoicer with zero customer-facing errors during a dual-write period of three weeks followed by a twelve-minute cutover. I also fixed flaky checkout tests blocking every deploy by creating a deterministic clock and seeded fixtures, dropping the flake rate from nine percent to zero.

## Incident Management and Tooling
I acted as incident commander for the INC-2291 ops-api brownout, where I identified a connection-pool leak, coordinated a rollback, and wrote the postmortem, with colleagues describing me as "The calmest IC I have seen in a while" because I provided clear updates every ten minutes. I cut paging noise down thirty-eight percent after auditing one hundred twelve alerts to delete twenty-nine and re-tune seventeen, reducing weekly pages from fifty-two to thirty-two. Additionally, I added a Slack acknowledgment button to the pager bot for one-click response and fixed an N+1 query on the crew roster endpoint that improved load time from 2.4 seconds to 140 milliseconds by preloading assignments.

## Developer Experience and Onboarding
I reduced the dev environment setup time from a full day to twenty-five minutes at Altimetry by converting a wiki page into a devcontainer and seed script, which allowed next two hires to use it on their first day. I shadowed the on-call rotation for two weeks before taking primary responsibility, writing a runbook PR that documented everything that confused me as a new on-call engineer, and made my first production change at Altimetry on day six by fixing timezone handling on crew duty reports to handle UTC versus local base time for day boundaries.

The quarter was defined by two massive migrations and a complete rebuild of our incident response process at Altimetry and Quillfeather, alongside launching new tooling for safety compliance and search performance.

## Search & Billing Reliability
I led the cutover for 41k subscriptions from the legacy invoicer to the new ledger without any customer-facing errors, a critical path that required a dual-write period and a precise 12-minute flip of the read paths [1]. I caught a proration rounding bug in the nightly reconciliation job before it could have affected 120 customers [8], while ensuring duplicate payment-provider webhooks never created duplicate invoices with idempotent handling [21]. I also shipped hybrid ranking to Quillfeather where search click-through rose by 14% and zero-result queries dropped by a third, keeping p95 latency under the 180 ms budget [2]. This was backed by moving embedding lookups to a warm cache and batching the re-ranker, which cut p95 latency from 410 ms to 160 ms; Theo Park noted in #search that "That latency graph is the nicest thing I have seen all quarter" [4]. We validated this with an offline evaluation harness running in CI in 6 minutes that showed the hybrid approach beats BM25 on every segment, including long-tail queries, after two weeks of testing over 1.2M sessions [9][13]. The foundation allowed Theo and me to co-write a blog post on the work that reached 9k reads in the first week [20]. I also implemented query logging with hashed identifiers and redaction so our eval set could be built legally [22].

## Altimetry Operations & Safety
I managed INC-2291, an ops-api brownout lasting 47 minutes where I identified a connection-pool leak, coordinated a rollback, and wrote the postmortem; Rafael Ortiz described me in #incidents as the "calmest IC I have seen in a while" who provided "clear updates every 10 minutes" [7]. I engineered a pager bot that collects pages, deploys, and Slack decisions into one timeline document, cutting postmortem prep time from half a day to 20 minutes; Oskar Lindqvist shared this achievement in chat about the export [6]. I fixed an N+1 query issue on the crew roster endpoint for Altimetry ops-api, preloading assignments to drop response times from 2.4 s to 140 ms [23]. To support our ground operations, I demonstrated offline sync at the company all-hands on stage with a tablet in airplane mode; Rafael Ortiz responded in #all-hands with "Airplane mode, live, on stage. Respect" after watching me run the demo [15]. This capability survived its first real weekend when crews at the pilot base ran 140 checklists over flaky hangar Wi-Fi with zero sync conflicts and zero lost sign-offs; Imani Brooks praised the offline sync in a chat message [3]. I delivered the first usable build of the tablet checklist for pilots, featuring big tap targets, glove mode, and sunlight readability, based on Sun-hee Lim's feedback about "glove-friendly" interaction [10].

## Search Relevance v2
I shipped hybrid ranking to 100% with a p95 latency under the budget while search click-through rose 14% and zero-result queries dropped by a third [2]. I also implemented an offline evaluation harness in CI that runs nDCG@10 on 4k judged queries in six minutes, allowing the team to argue with numbers instead of vibes [9], and confirmed via A/B testing that hybrid ranking beats BM25 across every segment during a two-week trial covering 1.2M sessions [13].

I led a dual-write implementation for the migration budget, paying for the latency costs by moving embedding lookups behind a warm cache and batching the re-ranker [4]. Theo Park called "That latency graph is the nicest thing I have seen all quarter" while viewing it in #search [4]. My work was documented in a blog post co-written with Theo titled How we rebuilt search ranking, which saw 9k reads in its first week and was picked up by two newsletters [20].

A key part of this project was moving from BM25 to hybrid ranking, where an A/B test over the past weeks showed that hybrid ranking beats BM25 on every segment, with the biggest win occurring on long-tail queries [13]. I moved embedding lookups behind a warm cache and batched the re-ranker in a pull request for quillfeather-example/search-service#1204 to ensure the budget was paid for while maintaining performance [4].
